title: VisHead-Spec: Head-Routed Visual Attention for Multimodal Speculative Decoding
abstract: arXiv:2611.21839v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Speculative decoding accelerates vision-language models(VLMs) while preserving the target model's outputs, but its speedup diminishes under high concurrency serving as the system becomes more compute bounded as the batch size increases. This problem is pronounced for multimodal speculative decoding as the long range of the image tokens in the prompt can significantly increase the computational cost during draft token prediction. The block-diffusion drafters (e.g. DFlash, DSpark) can effectively speed up the draft model efficiency by predicting multiple draft tokens in one forward pass, but their speedup for VLMs under high concurrency is still modest (<9%). translated_title: VisHead-Spec：面向多模态投机解码的头路由视觉注意力
translated_abstract: 投机解码能够在保持目标模型输出不变的前提下加速视觉语言模型（VLM），但在高并发服务场景下，随着批处理规模的增大，系统越来越受计算能力限制，其加速效果随之减弱。这一问题在多模态投机解码中尤为突出，因为提示词中图像token的长序列会显著增加草稿token预测阶段的计算成本。块扩散式草稿模型（如DFlash、DSpark）可以通过一次前向传播预测多个草稿token来有效提升草稿模型的效率，但它们在高并发下对VLM的加速效果仍然有限（不足9%）。为了理解这一差距，我们研究了从目标模型到草稿模型之间不同模态的信息流，并识别出目标模型与草稿模型之间视觉注意力的稀疏模式：草稿模型中只有一小部分键值头需要直接接收目标模型的视觉注意力信息……
tldr: 该论文提出VisHead-Spec，通过发现草稿模型中仅需少量键值头直接接收目标模型视觉注意力的稀疏模式，实现了高并发场景下依然高效的多模态投机解码加速。
en_tdlr: VisHead-Spec identifies a sparsity pattern in visual attention between target and draft models—only a small set of key-value heads in the draft model require direct visual attention routing—enabling effective multimodal speculative decoding acceleration even under high-concurrency serving.
